Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.
EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE POLICY: Teach a practical lesson without mentioning or selling the product. A useful independent takeaway is mandatory. Do not invent a personal experience.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600) and 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. Its one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. Give a specific reason to swipe through a tension, outcome, contrast, mistake, useful promise, or curiosity gap.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Slides 2-6 body copy must each be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. lessons.problem: Content creation feels like an endless cycle with no relief in sight.

lessons.problem: Starting each post from a blank page can feel daunting and unproductive.

lessons.problem: Logging meals can be a source of stress rather than support.
lessons.mistakenAssumption: Meal logging has to be time-consuming and complicated.
lessons.lesson: Convenient meal tracking methods can help reduce stress.
lessons.productMechanism: Record food by meal photo, barcode scan or description.
lessons.practicalAction: Use the photo logging feature to quickly capture your meal in the cafeteria.
lessons.takeaway: Simplifying the logging process can alleviate anxiety about tracking meals.
lessons.limitations: Photo analysis is about 80% accurate; ensure good lighting for better results.

lessons.problem: Family meals complicate personal meal logging.
lessons.mistakenAssumption: You must log every meal for every family member to track your own nutrition.
lessons.lesson: Multiple logging methods can simplify tracking amidst busy family life.
lessons.practicalAction: Log your personal meal by taking a quick photo while preparing dinner.
lessons.takeaway: You can focus on your own nutrition without the stress of logging every family member's meal.
lessons.limitations: Nutrition estimates can vary; clear focused photos help but do not ensure exactness.

lessons.problem: Relying on estimates can create uncertainty about progress.
lessons.mistakenAssumption: All meal logging methods provide equally accurate results.
lessons.lesson: Understanding the variability in estimates can help users make better choices.

lessons.practicalAction: Double-check the nutritional values of your homemade recipe by comparing it with similar entries.
lessons.takeaway: Being aware of the variability in estimates allows for more informed dietary choices.
lessons.limitations: Nutrition values can still vary widely; always consider this when logging.

lessons.lesson: Offering multiple input methods can alleviate decision fatigue.
lessons.productMechanism: Record food by meal photo, barcode scan or description.
lessons.practicalAction: Try logging your next meal by taking a photo instead of manually entering it.
lessons.takeaway: Experimenting with different logging methods can make tracking feel less daunting.
lessons.limitations: Photo analysis accuracy may vary; ensure good conditions for best results.
